_note: Paired statements (Pew-style forced choice), not agree/disagree. a = the side a candidate stance of "agree" means; b = "disagree". The quiz shows a/b in random order. Where a choice has a real cost, both sides name it. level: state = Governor, federal = US House, both = asked for both. short: true = in the quick quiz.

issues.context: Pennsylvania's minimum wage is the federal minimum, $7.25 an hour.
issues.a: Raise the state minimum wage, even if some businesses raise prices or cut hours.
issues.b: Keep it at $7.25, even if low-wage workers fall further behind rising costs.

issues.a: Use state money for scholarships so students can attend private schools.
issues.b: Keep state education money in public schools.

issues.a: Legalize and tax recreational marijuana for adults.
issues.b: Keep recreational marijuana illegal, even if that means giving up the tax money.

issues.context: Local property taxes pay a large share of public school costs.
issues.a: Cut or end school property taxes, even if that means higher state income or sales taxes to fund schools.
issues.b: Keep school property taxes, rather than shift the cost to higher state income or sales taxes.

issues.context: The state budget already spends more than it takes in.
issues.a: Give public transit like SEPTA steady new state funding, even with the budget gap.
issues.b: Hold off on new transit money, even if that means service cuts or higher fares.

issues.context: Pennsylvania is a top natural gas producer. Some states charge power plants for carbon pollution through a program called RGGI.
issues.a: Put growing natural gas and energy jobs first, even if that means more carbon pollution.
issues.b: Charge power plants for carbon pollution to fight climate change, even if electric bills go up.

issues.context: Right now only registered Democrats and Republicans can vote in their party's primary.
issues.a: Let independent voters vote in primary elections.
issues.b: Keep primaries for party members, so each party picks its own nominees.

issues.a: Abortion access should be protected by law.
issues.b: Lawmakers should be able to restrict abortion.

issues.a: State and local police should help federal immigration agents (ICE) find and detain people.
issues.b: Local police should leave immigration enforcement to federal agents.

issues.context: Right now, Pennsylvania asks for ID only from people voting at their polling place for the first time.
issues.a: Require every voter to show photo ID at every election.
issues.b: Keep the current rules, so eligible voters without photo ID aren't turned away.

issues.a: Require background checks on all gun sales, and let courts temporarily remove guns from people found to be a danger.
issues.b: Don't add these gun laws; enforce the ones already on the books.

issues.a: Set term limits for lawmakers and ban them from trading individual stocks.
issues.b: Let voters decide how long lawmakers serve, and keep current stock-trading rules.

issues.a: Keep broad tariffs on imports to bring back American jobs, even if prices go up.
issues.b: Roll back broad tariffs to lower prices, and use targeted tariffs only where needed.

issues.context: Extra federal help paying for ACA (Obamacare) plans, added in 2021, lapsed at the end of 2025.
issues.a: Extend or restore the extra help, even though it adds to federal spending.
issues.b: Don't extend it, to save federal money, even if premiums go up for some people.

issues.a: Reduce federal Medicaid spending and add work requirements, even if some people lose coverage.
issues.b: Protect Medicaid funding, even though it adds to federal spending.
